1. Go to your steam library.
2. Right click 'Marvel's Spider-man Remastered'.
3. Click 'Properties'. 
4. On the first tab 'GENERAL', scroll to the bottom called 'LAUNCH OPTIONS'.
5. In the text box,  type in "-nolauncher" without the " " quote. 
6. Close the Properties box. The next time you launch your game, it will skip the launch menu and start the game right away. 

Cheers!

I have way too many hours in this game. And I have 100% it so I know a little bit about the game. I have replayed it 6 times and it's so much fun in all the ways you expect and all the ways you didn't. I'll break it down for ya.

Expected: 

The Swinging. My goodness the swinging mechanics are so damn good that I genuinely feel like the web-head. I haven't played Mile Morales as I'm unsure about getting a game with slightly more polished mechanics for $40 and I can't ever find it for less than say $30. 

The Combat: Not as sharp as the Batman Arkham games but this is probably second. When you are in the zone, combat feels so clean. Especially when you use the environment.  

Story: It's one of the best pieces of Spider-man media out there. I don't know about Miles Morales or Spider-man 2 beyond the reviews. This is such a good story that is worthy of my 6 reruns. The DLC is ok, but it's got its moments. I just eat up any content this game has as it's so addictive. I won't spoil anything but you may find a few tears running down your face near the end of my main story. 

Unexpected: 

The Graphics are so incredible and so STABLE. My goodness, I can run the game on RTX max settings and still get 144hz but granted I use a 1080p 144hz monitor so dunno about 4k. However if you didn't have a Ray-Tracing GC but 4k, It would still run in the 200 fps range. 

Stealth Missions: Oh my goodness some of these missions are better than some Assassin Creed games. Granted its no HITMAN but it's REALLY good. At all the hideouts scattered around NYC I try to stealth them as much as the game will allow me as the animations for stealth take downs are so good that you wish you could do that the whole game. 

New York City: This is a fantastic world, that is the perfect jungle gym for Spidey. Everything from the details of the traffic, sidewalks, pedestrians and like Central Park to the massive iconic skyscrapers towering above the city are so well designed that you legitimately feel like you're in Manhattan. 

Literally the only negative I have for this game is the MJ missions. Nobody asked for MJ missions. I won't spoil anything but it's got the same feeling as the Batmo*tank* in Arkham Knight, it's only about 20-30% of the game but it does hinder the flow of the story and the gameplay. 

Overall review: 

FOR 100%ers: 9/10 Some achievements are a bit hard but not impossible. The taskmaster and freaking Screwball challenges on each difficulty are not required for 100% of in the game completion or the achievements. Just do em on easy and you're good to go.

For casuals:  10/10 One of the best story games I have played in a while and worth the $60. But maybe wait for the Christmas Sale as its now 2 or 3 years old on steam so it might get some big discount if your not a big superhero nerd like me. If you are, you will LOVE this game and all its little references and whatnot. 

I know I wrote a PHD Thesis on this but yeah...play it. Love you...

[h1] 8.5/10 [/h1]

Spider-man may not be the most famous, but definitely the most approachable superhero nowadays, not only did he win the love of the public, but his comics were also on the best-selling list of the superhero genre. It plays a significant role in the video game industry as well. Spider-Man: Web of Shadows, 2008, deeply influenced the famous game next year, Prototype, you could also see some of its design and mechanics in this work. The later two film adaptation games, The Amazing Spider-Man(2012) and The Amazing Spider-Man 2 (2014), though receiving mixed reviews, with their groundbreaking open-world settings and many creative game designs, deeply influence the Marvel Spiderman(2018). Compared to its original 2018 version, the remastered work fully upgrades its graphics. Though it does not alter the nature of its templated open-world AAA titles, it could still capture players with top-notch visuals, excellent combat design, and a smooth gaming experience.

Today's open-world AAA games commonly face a dilemma where the high degree of homogenization makes the so-called free exploration feel like a waste of time and energy, increasingly being criticized. The system of swinging through the city with spider webs, which was perfected in Spider-Man 2 (2004), has been continuously optimized in Spider-Man games, and this title takes it to new heights. Easy to pick up and thoroughly enjoyable, it balances a sense of speed, excitement, and exhilaration. This gameplay design, allowing players to roam and enjoy the day and night views of New York City, significantly reduces the fatigue and repetitiveness of traversing the map. In the game, players can freely choose the difficulty level, decide whether to skip some mini-games, and benefit from a very user-friendly auto-save mechanism. The in-game collectibles shown on the big map allow players to collect items easily without consulting a guide, and the effective game content mechanism ensures players almost never miss any storyline content. In terms of combat, the game retains the essence of past Spider-Man titles while simplifying operations and mechanics, yet still offers a high ceiling for player skill. With flexible character movements and the spider-sense mechanism, players can easily recreate highly spectacular combat scenes reminiscent of Spider-Man himself. Although the plot may seem clichéd and predictable, the overall tight pacing, grand scenes, and changes in the New York City environment as the story progresses allow players to immerse themselves fully, experiencing unparalleled excitement and chaos. Combined with excellent character voice acting, the experience is top-notch.

Not every player is fully aware of Spider-Man and his universe, characters included. On this note, the storyline of this game is set eight years after Peter Parker has become Spider-Man. While there are some additions to the previous storyline, world, and characters, they are overall rather fragmented, which might leave players unfamiliar with the IP feeling somewhat confused during gameplay. Undeniably, the storyline is emotionally impactful and has strong tension at its climax, but the overall plot is too condensed, resulting in a lack of development. Many characters are not well-developed, the villain characters lack appeal, and most characters' personalities are extremely biased. This makes their motivations understandable but hastily and superficially explained, leading to a poor experience for the player. The simplification of the combat system also leads to reduced content, and players might find the combat experience repetitive and mechanical in the mid to late stages of the game. Excessive use of long shots and slow motion in combat, especially during finisher, can cause aesthetic fatigue. As a templated open-world AAA game, it features a multitude of highly repetitive side missions, crime events, and base missions. While these may initially offer some immersion, they become increasingly boring as the game progresses. The design of challenge missions is poor, and the stealth content and puzzles added to the main storyline to expand gameplay often repel players. The DLCs are mediocre in terms of storyline, and while there is an effort to introduce different gameplay in side missions, it only serves as old wine in a new bottle, resulting in a frustrating experience for players. The game also has optimization issues, including occasional frame drops and various bugs.

It's undeniable that Marvel's Spider-Man: Remastered has indeed made transformative changes in terms of gameplay. Although it remains within the confines of a templated open-world framework, it still has commendable aspects. If you're highly interested in the gameplay of this title or are a fan of the Spider-Man series, this game won't disappoint. For about the price of a Spider-Man movie ticket, Marvel's Spider-Man: Remastered can offer you an experience as compelling as a film's storyline, exhilarating combat, and the thrill of swinging through New York City. It might currently be one of the best superhero games available. However, due to the highly repetitive design of side missions, unless you thoroughly enjoy the game's content, there's no need to aim for 100% completion; experiencing the main storyline is sufficient. Conversely, if you value gameplay over stunning visuals and dislike highly repetitive level designs, or if you've just finished a highly repetitive assembly-line AAA title, Marvel's Spider-Man: Remastered might not be for you. It's worth mentioning that only Act 3 of the main storyline and DLC 3 are particularly challenging, and while a controller can offer a superior immersive experience through haptic feedback, keyboard and mouse are the easiest to pick up and master.

After 45 hours, i've finished the main campaign, side-quests and the DLCs and i had a blast playing through all of them.

Spider-Man doesn't tell an origin story, it throws you right into action, with Spider-Man being an established character having fought bad guys for years already. Which isn't a bad thing, but beware if you aren't familiar with Spider-Man at all, it might be a bit confusing at first if you don't know who is who.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2853365498

In the game, you're playing Spider-Man (obviously) swinging his way through New York, which is beautiful to look at by the way, dealing with all sorts of crimes, challenges, side- and main-quests.
The main quest is the heart of the game, it's introducing the main villain and secondary villain, it got character development, humour, drama and heartbreak.
It's not groundbreaking and at times predictable, but it's a good story told pretty well. 
The relationship between Dr. Otto Octavius and Peter Parker, both working together in a lab, is explored and gives depth to both characters and gives the inevitable descend into madness from Otto more impact.
There's also Mr. Negative as antagonist, which is more of a one-dimensional character, but he works in the context of the game. Not good, not bad either.
Other Spidey villains have more of a secondary role as mini-bosses. It's fine, though a bit more depth would have served them well, instead of just throwing them at the player as a villain for 5 minutes. They felt thrown in for good measure, cause they're Spider-Man villains and the game needed mini-bosses, but because of that, they're flat, bland and interchangable.

Swinging and fighting is pretty easy, with Keyboard and Mouse controls working pretty well.
Traversing through the city is as easy as "hold to swing" with the occasional jump in between, or pulling yourself towards a surface and then jumping off with a boosted jump, giving you the necessary momentum to swing again.
There's also a wide variety of options to fight bad guys. The main attack kicks and punches the bad guys, but you can also fling them into the air, use any of your various gadgets, shoot your web at enemies and throw them onto others or onto the wall, stun them with electricity, push them off a rooftop with a sonic blast and other neat little things.
Dodging is important, perfect dodging even more so as it gives you a little slow-mo effect, which gives you time to get out of a tough situation, it's also relatively easy to pull off, as your Spidey-Sense is giving you an indication of when to dodge.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2853747441

Every now and then, you're also controlling another character (MJ or Miles Morales). These small sections usually require you to sneak around and be stealthy, so you don't alert any guards. I didn't hate them, i just wish it would have been more than just "sneak around". Story-wise they made sense, gameplay-wise they were "meh".

Besides the main story, there's also things scattered around the city, which are unlocked throughout the game. This ranges from simple crimes you need to stop (car chases, muggings or robberies) though these play relatively same-y, as it's mostly just bashing bad guys.
There are also challenges you can do, given to you by Taskmaster or Screwball for example, where you have to fight a certain amount of bad guys within a time limit and/or with specific gadgets, finding bombs scattered through the city also with a time limit and other similar things.
They're okay, they give a bit of variety, but they're also mostly typical flat side-content. 
Every now and then, there's also a little side-quest with an actual little story-arc, with some of them being quite interesting, though they never reach the depth of the main quest.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2853747262

Visually, the game is great. Swinging through the city gives you plenty opportunity to take some awesome screenshots with the photo mode. The city is full of pedestrians, cars, birds, planes and boats all giving you the illusion of a living and breathing city.
If you're on (or close to) the ground, you can also hear people cheering at you or simply asking you to "do the hand-thing", making the Spider-Man feel even more immersive.

Doing any quest or challenge rewards you with XP and gathering enough will level you up, giving you the opportunity to unlock new skills and also suits, and there are plenty to unlock throughout the game.

Overall, it's a great game with minor flaws. Technically, i didn't had much issues other than the audio not working twice, which a simple game restart fixed and with the generous checkpoints, there was no backtracking needed.
Sometimes controls seemed a bit finicky, but that might just be my own skill, or lack thereof.
Spider-Man is a visually fantastic game, with good moment-to-moment gameplay, a city that feels alive (even if it's just surface level) and a story (and DLCs) that is interesting and gives you plenty of reason to play through.
Highly recommended!

If you're wondering how this game runs on Steam Deck, let me just tell you its a dream out of the box. It feels almost native and is a blast to play. I'm a fan of Super Hero games, and I know my hours on record is low, but because I primarily play my Steam Deck offline, the hours on record are very off, at the time of writing this review. I am about 40 hours into the game. I've played it both on my Deck and on my gaming laptop, and the game runs very well on both. 

I've played the Arkham trilogy and Guardians of the Galaxy, and loved both. I would say this game is closer to the Arkham trilogy in its combat and overall objectives. The open world map is Manhattan, the main island that makes up New York City. The map is littered with little things for you to do, such as fighting criminals, taking pictures of landmarks, both real and part of the Marvel universe, and scientific stations where you complete an optional task. The more you progress in the game, the more things you unlock on the map. And I have not felt that anything was tedious to get, as I've cleared everything on the map up to this point. 

The story is very interesting, the voice acting is great, it's very fun to swing around the city, even though fast travel is an option, I do find myself swinging about 70% of the time. 

I would recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of Spider-Man and a fan of Marvel. Even to anyone who loves open world games.

Edit: Coming back to my review after 100% the game and it's DLCs. Still strongly recommend it if you're into super hero or open world games. Ran great the whole time on my Steam Deck. Does drain the battery though, but that's to be expected.

[i]Marvel’s Spider-Man Remastered[/i] is just ... it's just pure fun. Like, the game is eager and upfront about wanting the player to [i]feel[/i] like a superhero and be [i]cool[/i] and [i]have fun[/i]. Oh, to be young again. 

I mean, I could honestly leave the review at that. But seriously, I never saw the appeal of Spider-Man (also, I thought it was "Spiderman?"). Peter Parker seemed like a nice kid, but he doesn't have Batman's or Superman's aura. His powers also seemed weak—shooting webs and gymnastics can't hold a candle to Batman's fancy technology or Superman's literal superpowers. But I get it now! I do! There's a sense of limitless joy in the gameplay. The gameplay is addictive and reminiscent of the [i]Arkham[/i] series; the story and cast are surprisingly likable; and the game is great on Deck. I do have to point out, however, the game's repetitive nature. The map is filled with Ubisoft-style challenges that require multiple stages of completion. The side content is also noticeably weak, and though I had a blast, I'm going to deem [i]Spider-Man[/i] completed at around the 70% mark.

[b][h2]Pros:[/h2][/b]
✅ [b]Action.[/b] The combat is clearly inspired by the Batman games, but it carves out its own identity through Spider-Man's gadgets, web abilities, and incredible mobility. It's a pretty familiar formula: fast, fluid fights that reward combos. Yet it encourages you to mix attacks, gadgets, air combos, and environmental takedowns instead of relying on a single strategy. Usually, games put the most love into the physical combat, but I honestly relied on Spidey's gadgets half the time—they're STRONG. 

✅ [b]Traversal.[/b] I usually hate the "empty air" nature of traveling in open-world games. Just get me to my location, godDAMN. I only enjoyed [i]Dying Light[/i] and [i]Batman[/i]'s traversal because of the importance of XP, side content, or mechanics. But Spidey's web-slinging through New York City never stopped being entertaining! I feel like there are some hidden mechanics going on wrt speed, height, location, freedom, and momentum. There's a difference between crawling up a wall, slinging around a corner, or being catapulted into the air. Fast travel almost feels unnecessary because getting there is half the fun.

✅ [b]Surprisingly likeable cast[/b]. I'm not familiar with the original material, so I didn't expect to get invested in the characters. Still, Peter, MJ, Miles, Aunt May, Otto, and the supporting cast all won me over. I was particularly impressed with Otto. In the game, he seems like such a sweet old dude, but his descent into becoming a familiar villain was a neat callback. The writing also strikes a nice balance between lighthearted humor and emotional moments. It focuses strongly on relationships (Peter/MJ; Peter/Miles), grief (Peter; Aunt May; Miles), and justice. The story was surprisingly good, too!

✅ [b]DLCs are included.[/b] Having [i]The City That Never Sleeps [/i]bundled into the remastered version is a nice bonus and adds several more hours of content without needing additional purchases.

✅ [b]Excellent Steam Deck performance.[/b] Controls feel smooth, performance is a solid 45 FPS, and the game translates remarkably well to handheld play.

[b][h2]Cons:[/h2][/b]
🟥 [b]Repetitive open-world content.[/b] Once the novelty wears off, the map starts to resemble the typical Ubisoft formula. Enemy bases, research stations, radio stations, backpacks, landmarks, crimes, challenges—most activities are enjoyable individually, but there are simply too many of them. I did enjoy the radio stations, landmarks, and backpacks, but I was not a fan of the rest. The game felt bloated because there would always be a new activity or situation that you would need to go through 10 to 30 icons for a small reward. The fact that the city isn't diverse enough doesn't help.

Combat is impactful and responsive, clearly inspired by the Batman Arkham series, but with its own acrobatic twist. Hits land with weight, gadgets add creativity, and chaining together aerial combos feels fantastic. That said, the core melee can become repetitive toward the endgame. Without mixing in gadgets and environmental tools, fights can start to feel a bit samey. When you do use the full toolkit, though, combat becomes far more dynamic and enjoyable. Stealth is present and functional, but it doesn’t quite reach the heights of the Arkham games. The story is solid and emotionally driven, the performances particularly Peter and certain major antagonists  are strong, and the narrative has some genuinely powerful moments. [h1] I’m not really into superhero games but... [/h1]

...Spider-Man Remastered (SMR) has got to be one of the best story-driven games I have ever played. This game feels like a movie, the graphics, the sound, dialogue, characters, everything just blew me away. If you’ve not already played it, I hope my review can persuade you to get it, you won’t regret it. 

[h3] The most beautiful game I’ve ever played (?) [/h3]

So first of all, I’m playing this game on a 7800X3D and a 4080 Super. That means that I could turn every graphics setting to the max and play with full on ray-tracing. SMR plays insanely well, even with everything turned up, steady 95-100 FPS, no crazy drops or glitches. This game looks like a movie, there’s no difference to some of the cutscenes and playing the game. I’ve posted some screenshots which you can check out on my profile if you want to. The last couple of games I’ve played were originally released on PS as well (The Last of Us Part 1, Ghost of Tsushima) but SMR looks even better to the games I’ve played before. 

The details are insane, every building looks different, details inside some offices crazy. I won’t spoil anything but the lab Peter’s working in is something to behold, there’s so much going on, I just walked around for like 20 minutes trying to take every little detail in. And each location feels like this vibrant and real place which you get to explore, a-ma-zing.

[h3] Gameplay [/h3]

This is my first Spider-Man game experience ever, so I was kind of hesitant how I’d like the web-slinging element, but the implementation is great. I’ve played SMR with a DualSense controller (which it fully supports) and the button mapping feels natural from the start. The game guides you through all the moves during exploring, fighting and solving puzzles. Once you get the hang of certain mechanics the pop-ups to help you also disappear which I really like. 

When you’re not busy swinging through the city you’re busy fighting or exploring inside buildings. The fighting feels so flexible, Spidey can do a wide variety of moves, Spidey-sense helps to let you know when to dodge an attack, he’s like this master of agility and resourcefulness with using his surroundings to win fights. You can pick up and throw stuff at your enemies, use their own attacks against them, chose a more stealth approach or just go all-out and play it more in a fighting-type style game. Last but not least there are some puzzles, which are never too hard but give a decent challenge.

[h3] (The attention to detail of) The Sound [/h3]
Maybe the thing that blew me away most about SMR is the sound. There are so many little details that you hear after playing awhile. Like, when Peter’s in a dialogue with someone calling him, when you’re stationary his voice sounds like his regular self. But when choosing to start webslinging somewhere during the conversation his voice changes, you can hear he needs to use his strength with each sling he does. When he starts slinging up and thus using his muscles to gain momentum you can actually hear his voice changing in the conversation he’s having. To me that’s such a specific part the developer paid attention to, amazing.

There’s so much more, the way the wind sounds when you’re in slinging in between buildings, the way it sounds different if you’re at a more open space. The dialogue speech is a-tier (a+++++), no matter how tiny a role a character plays they really give it their all to make you feel their emotion. Lip-syncing could not have been done better, basically you’re in a movie.

[h3] The Story (is awesome) [/h3]

Look, I know it’s practically cursing when you’re a gamer but, I’m not the biggest fan of superheroes. My hero from when I was younger was Tintin, I was less about the action and more about the adventure and exploring. I’ve watched some of the Spider-Man movies, tried Iron-Man and a couple of others but it’s not really for me. But I think I might have to give the new Spider-Man movies another try, he really is an amazing superhero. 

This game really plays like a movie, the story is so good. The way you’re introduced to each of the characters. You don’t need any knowledge about earlier games, movies or the comic itself to be able to enjoy it. Sure, it helps with some of the context the game is giving you, but you can enjoy it just as well as a standalone experience of the Spider-Man universe. The game takes it’s time to introduce different characters, and it’s entirely up to you if you want to advance the main story or if you choose one of the side-stories to get a more in-depth look into the world of Spider-Man. My first playthrough (which took me about 25 hours) was more focused on the main-storyline but I will definitely play through it another time to get all the side-story missions done, it’s well worth it.

[h3] Some small notions [/h3]

If you’ve read some of my other reviews than it comes as no surprise that I’m not too big a fan of big maps with too much to do on them. Unfortunately, SMR throws an insane amount of explorable, unlockable options at you. Sure, some are needed to upgrade your gear and also give you XP but it’s too much. This game would’ve been fine with having half of all those options, the city is interesting enough to have an icon appear every 10 building you pass with something to do. It feels like filler to extent the hours you put into the game, it doesn’t need it, 25-30 hours is fine for this type of game.

Also I’ve had multiple times where I was somehow able to get stuck inside of a building I wasn’t supposed to get into. Like ghosting through a wall, not being able to get out and having to restart from an earlier checkpoint (which is like a loss of 3 minutes of gameplay, so no big issue). I happened twice in my total playthrough, so nothing too crazy.  

[h3] Top 10? [/h3]

There are so many games that are worth playing at least once in your life, I’d rate SMR to be in the top 25 somewhere on that list for sure. I have played many hundreds of games in my 30+ years of gaming and I think SMR comes really (like really reallllly) close to my top 10 games I’ve ever played. The thing is, my top 10 is always changing but it tells me this game really is that good. 

The fact that we’re in this age of gaming where so many games can make you feel like you’re a part of this amazing journey, with great graphics, sound, storylines, it makes it so difficult to choose where you want to spent your time on. But I can’t recommend SMR enough, if you had to choose to play like 5 games for the year, this would be one of them. 

Hope I’ve somewhat helped with your purchase decision. 

Love,

PJ

[h2]Some Childhood Thoughts[/h2]
I remember always wanting to play Amazing Spider-Man 2 on Windows 7 as a kid, but coming from a lower income household, my parents could never afford it. I was pretty excited when they bought me some knockoff DVD to try and install, but sadly it never worked out. Growing up, that specific excitement faded away over time. Although Insomniac's Spider-Man was not able to fully recreate that childhood innocence, it completely encapsulates everything I ever wanted in a superhero game. The cinematic execution and storytelling are breathtaking, and I loved every chapter the main campaign had to offer.

[h2]Gameplay Thoughts[/h2]
The open-world experience is incredibly addicting. Swinging through a beautifully recreated New York City feels fluid and natural. It is so fun that you will likely still prefer swinging to objectives even after you unlock Fast Travel. The combat takes heavy inspiration from the Arkham series, focusing on acrobatic dodging, building up a combo meter, and utilizing a fun arsenal of web gadgets. The side quests and random street crimes can become repetitive and boring after a while, but this fatigue only really set in for me far into New Game Plus. It is also worth noting that this Remastered edition includes all DLCs.

[h2]A Flawless PC Port & Verdict[/h2]
Sony and Nixxes Software have delivered what has to be one of the best ports I have ever played. It is surprisingly well optimized for PC and runs perfectly on the Steam Deck. You get a plethora of settings to tweak, from ultra-wide monitor support to unlocked framerates and ray-tracing options. Whether you want to push your high end rig to the visual limit or just want a stable experience on a handheld device, the game scales great.

Overall, the journey was amazing. The repetitive side content might pad out the runtime for completionists, but the core web-swinging and engaging narrative make this an absolute must-play. Extremely Recommended!

Marvel’s Spider-Man Remastered

I just wrapped another playthrough of Marvel’s Spider-Man Remastered, and honestly, it hit even harder this time around. After first playing it on PlayStation a couple of years back, trying it again on my Steam Deck was like rediscovering what made me fall in love with it first time.

The main story is where the game shines - and honestly ending made me cry like a baby. It took me about 15 hours, and I was glued to the screen the entire time (sorry boss, work can wait). Every character moment landed, every fight felt punchy, and swinging through New York… it’s the kind of thing that makes you feel like a kid again (I grew up on Spider-Man cartoons).

The side stuff is actually worth and fun doing. There’s about five more hours of collecting, helping random citizens, and cleaning up the city. Some games make this stuff feel like a chore, but here it’s just pure fun—another excuse to swing around, discover some easter eggs from marvel universe and enjoy that sweet web-slinging.

Then come the DLCs, which tacked on another 15 hours for me. Each of them (3 in total) felt like a bonus chapter rather than filler, with their own villains and storyline. It’s the perfect way to extend the gameplay experience.

The Steam Deck handled everything surprisingly well. I didn’t have trouble with controls or performance (next will test Miles Morales, that I have never played before)—the whole thing looked and played great handheld. 

Four days, and that was pretty much all I did. The game makes it ridiculously easy to lose track of time—not because it’s demanding, but because it’s genuinely joyful to play. 

If you grew up loving Spider-Man or just like open-world games with a bit of heart and humor, this one’s absolutely worth your time.

10/10 from me

Marvelᵀᴹ Spider-Man Remastered is a great looking game that has some serious flaws in its soulless gameplay loop.

[b]What I like about this game?[/b]
+ The game looks great and runs at constant 60fps on my i7-9700k and RTX 2070 on 1080p at max settings with RTX disabled.
+ Being a Spider-Man has been mastered by this game. You can tsip, whip and tsap on the roofs of New York with multiple mechanics with seamless transitions from web slinging to street swinging.
+ Animation work is great overall. There are lots of references to various classic Spider-Man poses and moves.
+ Voice acting in this game is extremely professional with lots of dialogue from various characters. John Jonah Jameson's radio show with the Alex Jones undertones and Dan Slott's comic inspiration is the highlight for me.
+ Writing on the script is a refreshing take on Spider-Man. It contains a lot of comic inspirations from classic stories to more modern Marvel and I like pretty much all of the characters. I especially like how classic Mary Jane Watson got combined with the character of Betty Brant on this version. A logical and good move in order to make her more relevant to the story and do meaningful stuff.
+ Spider-Man has lots of gadgets that are fun to use and look great.
+ There are lot of side missions and content, which is a plus but also a big minus when it comes to its quality.
+ There are lots of unlockables, if you like that kind of content.

[b]What I don't like about this game[/b]
- The gameplay is extremely repetitive. Most of the missions consist of classic and boring open world game tropes; activating a radio tower or other static object, going from point A to point B, collecting items scattered across the game world, scripted chase scenes etc. There's nothing innovative in this game when it comes to its open world gameplay implementation, if you don't count the web-swinging.
- The game world feels lifeless both in design and lore. There are lot of easter egg references to a more wide Marvel universe and its characters, but it's very MCU synergy limited. Nothing interesting also happens in the game world, as you keep encountering the same 5-6 crime activities with the same enemies. Pedestrians also do almost nothing and the streets are scarcely populated, though I blame this on PS4 hardware limitations.
- Enemy variation in this game is very bad. There are 3 different kind of enemies (melee, gun, big tanky class) with minor sub-classes when it comes to their equipment (melee with object, sword, whip and shield. Gun with rifle, sniper and rocket). You encounter these same enemy types throughout the game with different skins.
- Combat in this game gets boring fast, as it's way too forgiving after you've leveled up and gotten some good skills and perks. It is also way too simple and repetitive for longer play sessions.
- The unavoidable stealth sections where you play as Mary Jane Watson or Miles Morales are some of the worst designed stealth sections I've played in any game. They're super linear and the AI on these parts is bad and immersion breaking, as they can't see or hear a person one meter in front of or behind them. The AI also gets very buggy at times on these sections. Worst of all, these parts break the action and even story flow of the game.
- The constant mini-game bombardment. They're actually fun brain puzzles, but too much is too much and just adds bloat to the game and also breaks the story flow.
- Web-swinging controls are smooth, but wall and ground based movement not that much. There's a bit of a momentum delay when it comes to movement, which makes it sometimes surprisingly hard to make precise actions like landing to a certain spot or simply getting off the ledge.
- The game is a quick time event fest. Every cool thing that happens in the game from stopping cars to great cinematic moments are just quick time events. Even the boss battles in this game are glorified quick time events most of the time.

I'd give Spider-Man 6/10 as a game experience and 8/10 if you're hardcore Spider-Man fan like me. The initial experience and first couple of hours can be fun, but the repetition in its gameplay gets too much after a while. I completed about 70% of the game until I had to question myself if I'm actually having fun with the game and if it's enough to play the game to the end.

I'd recommend getting this game from a hefty sale.

Spider-Man 2018 was a highly anticipated game by Insomniac Games. They're mostly known for making games exclusive to PlayStation and they have a good reputation thanks to the Ratchet & Clank series. When I first watched that gameplay video of Spider-Man from E3 2016, I knew I was in for a treat. The swinging animations looked smooth, the characters were true to their origin, the action was on point, and the story looked interesting with several villains thrown into the same scenario. Martin Li is an obscure villain compared to well-known bad guys like Green Goblin, Doc Ock, Kingpin, etc. and it was quite exciting to see what Insomniac and Sony had up their sleeves. They were obviously trying to break out from the regular Spider-Man scenarios we've all seen through the years while maintaining the classic Spider-Man atmosphere. It was impossible for a Spidey fan not to feel excited about it.

Most of us here have a huge nostalgia for Sam Raimi's Trilogy and I can easily say that this game is a love letter to Spider-Man 2 for PS2 if you've ever got your hands on that game back when you were a kid. Most of you probably know that it was that game that invented the swinging mechanic this game uses. As expected from 2018's standards, it improves upon it. Until Spider-Man 2, webs were attached to the sky but Jamie Fristrom came up with the idea that it would be way more realistic if webs were attached to the buildings instead of the sky. Getting that trivial yet important information out of the way, let's talk about the game itself a bit.

Peter Parker is 23 years old in this game and he's been Spider-Man for 8 years. In other words, this is not an origin game, he's quite experienced as Spider-Man in this story and apparently, he has a beef with Wilson Fisk a.k.a. Kingpin for a long time. The game starts off by sending you to take down Fisk, and after that, it slowly teaches you about the side missions, certain mechanics, and such stuff. There are several side missions and side activities for you to take on and they are fun to do most of the time. Some of them get repetitive fast but you can easily avoid getting yourself bored to death by swinging onto another activity. Swinging is smooth but it's not fast enough for my liking and the freedom you have is not the same with the Spider-Man 2. In Spider-Man 2, I remember I was able to run on walls while holding a web but in this one, Spider-Man lets go of the web once you get in contact with a wall and starts running normally. Now I know this is nitpicking but come on! That was fun, man! Anyway, it balances out things with lots of other cool stuff to do while swinging, so no worries there. 

The combat and stealth are heavily inspired by Batman Arkham games and that's a very good thing since those are some of the best games out there. You have lots of gadgets to add variety to your stealthy approaches and to regular combat. Two of my favorites are Impact Web for combat and Trip Mine for stealth. Speaking of stealth, I extremely disliked how they designed some stealth challenges given by Taskmaster and Screwball. Speed and stealth don't mix well together and yet the faster you are, the more points you get. The urge to act fast usually leads to reckless behavior and it usually gets you in trouble. So yeah, those challenges are one of the few things I didn't like about the game. The game also crashes if you attempt to retry them after a failure. Speaking of technical issues of the game, the port is not the best. I'd suggest turning off RTX because ray-traced reflections run on a lot lower FPS compared to the game's speed and by that I mean if your game runs at solid 60 FPS, the reflections will be like 30 or something even lower. I don't know how Miles Morales performs in that regard but I heard it doesn't do a very good job at improving upon its predecessor. 

The story of the game is probably the best Spider-Man story I've ever seen. It's basically a perfect scenario. Each character has a great development and most of them are quite likeable and relatable. Except Mary Jane. Man, why does she have to be so annoying in every Spider-Man story!? She's not completely useless this time, I'll give her that but I hated her stealth sections! I hope they will never return in the next installment! Apart from her boring gameplay, her character is a Karen. She broke up with Peter because he didn't want her rushing into the den of the bad guys recklessly and risking her life and she thought that Peter was only happy when she was behind her laptop instead of thinking that he was worried because she doesn't have superpowers like him. That's not being a strong and independent woman, that's being dumb and reckless. Despite all that, Peter is simping really hard for her. I guess they're perfect for each other. Oh and, I hate the new face. John Bubniak was perfect. After 70 hours of gameplay, I couldn't get used to it.

Spider-Man 2018 is the perfect Spider-Man game and story you're looking for. It's quite fun to play and easy enough to attain a 100% completion rate. [i][h2]Marvel’s Spider-Man Remastered – My First Swing, and It Webbed Me In[/h2][/i]
This is honestly my first Spiderman game, so maybe I’m a bit biased towards my experience. It did a really good job of making you feel like a "superhero", Or more specifically, like Spiderman just doing his thing in NYC. There’s a nice balance of action, story, and those classic Spidey awkward/cringe moments that somehow work.

One thing I absolutely loved was the attention to detail. Whether it was J. Jonah Jameson's hilarious radio rants reacting to your actions, NPCs commenting as you walked by, or even the subway fast travel animations changing depending on what was happening in the story (like Peter hiding from Sable agents when he's being hunted), those little touches made New York feel alive.

The gameplay also leans into the "Spider" part of Spiderman really well. Traversal is satisfying, combat flows naturally, and there are so many moments where everything just clicks and makes you genuinely feel like Spiderman. The boss fights could’ve used more challenge (even on Ultimate difficulty, they were a bit too easy), but enemy variety was solid, and the general pacing of fights felt right not too overwhelming, not too dull.

The way Miles is introduced into the story was also fantastic. His cutscenes, dialogue, and interactions with Peter give you a heartfelt glimpse into how he's beginning his own journey. (I still haven't played Miles Morales at the time of writing this, but this game made me even more excited to jump into it.)

[h2]Performance[/h2]
Performance was unfortunately the weakest part of my experience.
On my RTX 4060 laptop, the game really didn't like alt-tabbing. It would go from a smooth 100+ FPS to a stuttery 20–50 FPS, which was incredibly frustrating. The same issue could also happen randomly after missions or during gameplay.

DLSS and Frame Generation also didn't seem to work properly for me. At 1440p, my FPS was almost identical whether they were enabled or disabled, and turning DLSS off actually resulted in smoother frame pacing.
[b]Edit:[/b] I was later informed that lowering Texture Quality from Ultra to High can help reduce the stuttering on an RTX 4060. I haven't personally tested it yet, but it may be worth trying if you're experiencing the same issue.

While this game definitely had it's moments, it took me many hours to understand what the underlying agitation was. My initial play through was a 100% run and the second on Ultimate difficulty.

The game is spectacle. Which is terrific if that's what you want from this game. Spiderman has really cool moves and works his way through really fun fights. However, I wanted a game where I was the one building my skill to perform cool attacks and be an amazing spiderman. That is not what this game is. You press the punch button until the bar fills, then you push the other button to perform a finisher. You are not learning cool combos or navigating fights in a way only spiderman could. You just sit back and watch the spectacle that someone else made. 

This also infects the web swinging. If you want to get across town, you push the swing button, then the jump button, then swing again. You don't have to pay attention to momentum or consider where the buildings are so that you can traverse a path. They added a zipline type ability so that if you mess up your swing, just zip back up and jump into a swing. This kind of hand holding is also evident when you jump off a tall building. You don't die, you just do a super hero landing. Not very interesting. I jumped off the tallest building to make sure it wasn't a fluke. Nope. No death. Don't worry about trying too hard. 

Boss fights aren't any better. Some are fun locations. Near the end of the game you have to fight two bosses at a time. Even on ultimate difficulty it only took one attempt, but just a few more punches. None of them had any interesting to do. You dodge, then attack, then wait for their attack combo to finish. Of all the legendary spiderman villains in the game, none of them do anything interesting to do. They all go through an almost identical pattern of attack.

At the very least, the game isn't bad. It's just not what I wanted to play so I spent many hours understanding what bothered me. The whole time I was hoping to have an option for a more technical experience after finding how many accessibility options were added.

[h1] A Heroic Tale [/h1] 

Spider-Man is an absolutely incredible game, that is full of love for the source material, and incredible fast paced gameplay. You can tell that the developers poured their heart and soul into this game and it rivals the Arkham games for the title of best superhero video game of all time. Fans of Spider-Man and people who have never read a single comic or seen a single movie will love every second of this title. I 100% this game and loved every second of it.

[h2] Presentation [/h2] 

Spider-Man looks absolutely gorgeous. Between the gorgeous graphics and stunning recreation of New York City, you'll lose track of time as you're immersed in this world that has been created. Swinging through the streets is an absolute joy and the character designs are incredible. The cutscenes look like they could be straight out of a movie and the sound design is just as good. The soundtrack is subtle when it needs to be and heroic during the intense moments. You feel the weight of the punches you throw and feel the wind in your face as you swing from roof to roof.

[h2] Story [/h2] 

The story here is just as good as the gameplay. You're taken on a journey of loss, grief, revenge, and everything in between. There's plenty of moments that hit you like a wrecking ball including one of the best endings to a game I've played. The writers truly understood what makes these characters beloved and adored by fans and the story gives you time to become invested in characters which adds to the pay off of the big story beats and emotional moments. The DLC story was weaker but still quite enjoyable. 

[h2] Gameplay [/h2] 

While everything else has been amazing, the gameplay is what elevates this title to legendary. The combat is so incredibly fluid and fast paced that you truly feel like a superhero. The way you're able to string together combos using gadgets and your mobility both in the air and on the ground feels SO good. You can use a variety of gadgets to aid you, as well as the environment by throwing objects at the enemies. As you play more and more you unlock upgrades and new abilities which only expand your possibilities on how to approach combat. If I had to nitpick, the MJ stealth sections were kind of weak, but not terrible. They just aren't as good as the rest of the game which is understandable. The movement is another aspect of the game that needs to be talked about though. Never before has a game made moving around the world so damn fun. Swinging through New York is SO FREAKING FUN!!! There's all kinds of moves you can do such as swinging, diving, launching yourself off of jumps, and once you get good, you can traverse the city effortlessly, with every move looking and feeling incredible. Movement becomes effortless after a while and you'll never want to fast travel again. There's plenty of side quests and collectibles as well, just expanding the cast of characters and villains you get to face off against. 

[h2] Conclusion [/h2] 

It's been a long time since I've played a game of this scale that I enjoyed this much. Every moment of web swinging action, and heartbreaking story telling will have you glued to the screen. I encountered very little performance issues, with only the odd stutter here and there. If you're a fan of Spider-Man buy this game. If you don't even know who Peter Parker is, buy this game. If you have a computer that can run it, buy this game. You won't regret it.
